title: Tidy tests/window: HF-010, HF-013, HF-027, HF-028
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: T-003's check 'VOID unless the taller window gave the tree more room than the default' fails on this PC's current display, because the default window already fills the 816 px work area. It fails the same way at HEAD, so `WindowCases.ps1 -Case All` exits 1 here whatever the code does. The check should report VOID (not FAIL) when the default window already fills the work area, or the case should say it needs a taller display.

The person-run network pass (docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md staleness rule) was already stale. This slice touches more of its watched paths: tests/window/FsaWindowHook/**, tests/window/StallRig/**, tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 and FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj. N-001..N-004 and StalledShareTests (O-030) are still owed to a person. StallRig was built here, but no network case was run.

WindowCases.ps1 still writes all-zero files outside New-File: the lone and denied-folder files near Test-B*, the long-path P-001 files, and New-HundredThousand. The New-CaseFolder refusal now covers them, but they would compress in a compressed folder if they were ever made outside a case folder.

Tree and reveal modes return before the hook's FSA_HOOK_RENAMED check, so either mode ignores the variable silently rather than refusing it. This does no harm, because neither mode reads the window's refresh state.
